code_name: Miami-Dade County Code of Ordinances, Chapter 33 Zoning
edition: Zoneomics mirror of the Code (zoneomics.com/code/miami-dade-county-unincorporated-FL), undated; read through an automated summarizer, so details may be lossy
caveats: Municode blocked automated access (403); all text is from the Zoneomics mirror, read through a summarizing fetch tool, so exact wording and some item numbers need verification on Municode.
Purpose statements are missing from the mirror for most districts; fields left null or marked not stated rather than guessed.
IU-1/IU-2/IU-3 do not state general lot size or coverage; setbacks come from Art. II 33-51 and height from Art. III 33-57/33-58 as summarized.
AU chapter: last ~24k characters (33-284 to 33-284.1) and opening of 33-280 were not read.
Residential (RU-1, RU-1MA, EU-M) setbacks, coverage and height not found. Minor-district entries are short by design.
Urban center districts share Art. XXXIII(K); regulating plans and the Table of Permitted Uses were not read. LCCUC appears as LCUC in the mirror.
Data centers are not named in any district article read; treat as not addressed everywhere. Chapter 13 (not Chapter 33) was reported to govern explosives use and storage; not read.
Overlays not read: Bird Road overlay (ch. 48), Rockmining overlay, airport zoning, Homestead Air Reserve Base zoning, which can restrict uses.

districts.name: Interim District
districts.purpose: Catch-all interim district covering all unincorporated land not placed in another district; regulations are set by the trend of development in the neighborhood rather than a fixed use list.
permitted_uses: No fixed use list. Inside the Urban Development Boundary (UDB): the Director applies the regulations of the predominant use class in the neighborhood; if no trend is established, EU-2 minimum standards apply (5 acres gross; EU-1/EU-2 uses: one-family residence, limited agriculture/animals).
Outside the UDB: land designated Agriculture on the CDMP follows the AU district; Open Land and Environmental Protection land follows the trend-of-development process.
Land designated Terminal in an Urban Expansion Area may have truck parking and related ancillary uses under IU-1 development standards with administrative site plan review.
Municipal parks and recreation facilities allowed inside the UDB; group homes up to 6 residents (1,000 ft spacing).
Data centers, explosives/energetics manufacturing, solar, outdoor storage: not addressed in the GU article itself (outcome depends on the district whose standards are applied).

standards.min_lot_size: 5 acres gross where no trend is established (EU-2 standards), unless the CDMP requires more; pre-April 12 1974 platted/deeded lots meeting EU-1 minimums may use EU-1 uses
standards.setbacks: Follow the district whose standards are applied (EU-2: buildings other than the residence 85 ft from highway right-of-way)
standards.other: EU-2 lot width 200 ft, depth 330 ft

districts.notes: GU is effectively a placeholder: the real answer needs a Director's trend-of-development determination per parcel. The GU article does not itself state height or coverage. A footnote refers to GU variances in 33-36(b).

districts.name: Agricultural District
districts.purpose: Agricultural district allowing farming, agritourism and agriculture-related uses on large lots, plus estate-type residential.
permitted_uses: Uses of RU-1, EU-M or EU-1 (except golf courses); bed and breakfast up to 6 rentable bedrooms
Barns/sheds, packing houses (small up to 3,500 sq ft; large on 10+ acres), grazing, poultry, dairy, aquaculture, farms, groves, greenhouses/nurseries, hydroponics, seed drying (10+ acres)
Commercial vehicle storage only in specified areas (Open Land Subarea 1 and an area east of the UDB), 10+ gross acres, annual operating permit, 8 ft wall/fence and paved surface (33-283.1)
Outdoor storage of farm equipment permitted if 50 ft from right-of-way; distribution vehicles capped at 0.4 per gross acre, max 200 per lot (33-279.3)
Rural event venues, farm stands, farm-related wineries/breweries/distilleries, agritourism, farmers markets, farm equipment sales, low-THC/medical cannabis dispensing
Solar facilities as a primary use are permitted (33-279 item 30); solar panel area does not count toward lot coverage; floating solar under 33-20(q)
Community composting with administrative approval; schools (250 ft setback); farm labor housing

Data centers: not addressed. Explosives manufacturing: not addressed (only fireworks mentioned, prohibited as noise violation). Truck terminals: not addressed except commercial/distribution vehicle storage above.
conditional_uses: Public hearing: barns within 250 ft of a residence/RU/EU; hog farms over 2 hogs per site; dairy barns near residences; dude ranches and riding academies; farm labor barracks; extra distribution vehicles by special exception

standards.min_lot_size: 5 acres including right-of-way for new lots, with 200 ft frontage; exceptions for pre-1974 platted lots, 1 acre/150 ft frontage lots, and 10,000 sq ft pre-1951 lots per Art. II
standards.max_height: 35 ft, two stories (agritourism structures 25 ft)
standards.setbacks: 1+ acre lots: front 50 ft, rear 25 ft, interior side 15 ft, side street 25 ft; accessory buildings: front 75 ft, rear 7.5 ft, side 20 ft, side street 30 ft; livestock 250 ft from residential district, hogs 500 ft from residence
standards.lot_coverage: 15% of lot for 1+ acre lots (25% for smaller excepted lots); poultry housing and certain nursery buildings exempt; solar panels excluded
standards.other: Min dwelling cubic content 7,500 cu ft; commercial vehicle storage setbacks 25 ft front/side/rear, 100 ft from water body

districts.notes: Purpose statement not found in the mirrored text. Opening text of 33-280 was truncated by the fetch tool; lot area figures taken from visible text plus Art. II (33-49/33-50). Last ~24k characters of the chapter (33-284 to 33-284.1) were not read.

districts.name: Governmental Property
districts.purpose: Overlay-type designation for government-owned land in fee simple that is used for the listed governmental purposes; reverts to the underlying district if the use ends.
permitted_uses: Public parks, playgrounds; fire and police stations; vehicle inspection stations
Public water and sewer treatment and distribution facilities; solid waste collection and disposal facilities
Libraries, civic buildings, community centers; public hospitals, nursing homes, health facilities; auditoriums, arenas, museums
Detention facilities; public maintenance and equipment yards; public bus/rapid transit facilities; public airports (subject to airport zoning); other similar governmental uses
Data centers, solar, explosives manufacturing, private outdoor storage: not addressed (district is for government-owned land)

standards.other: Development standards not stated in the mirrored text; the underlying zoning district applies

districts.notes: Described as an overlay zoning district applied in addition to underlying zoning. No conditional uses, purpose statement or dimensional standards found in the mirrored text.

districts.name: Industrial, Light Manufacturing District
districts.purpose: Light industrial district for manufacturing, wholesale and distribution, warehousing and related services. Purpose statement not found in the mirrored text.
permitted_uses: Light manufacturing and fabrication: machine shops, welding shops, steel fabrication, furniture manufacturing, cabinet/millwork shops, upholstery, printing, bottling, food processing (5+ employees), ice manufacturing, mattress manufacturing, textile mills, leather goods (no tanning)

Warehousing and storage: wholesale storage showrooms, cold storage, marine warehouses, membership and home-improvement warehouses, warehouses for BU products, storage garages for trucks, buses and heavy equipment, wood and coal yards, contractor offices and yards
Passenger and freight stations and terminals for boats, trucks, buses and railroads (item 59); commercial and noncommercial parking lots
Aircraft hangars, repair, assembly and manufacturing; new/used auto and truck sales, auto repair, auto/truck rental; shipyards and dry docks

Armories and arsenals (item 5); oxygen storage and cylinder filling; pharmaceutical storage; fertilizer and insecticide mixing/storage (asterisked, hearing if within 500 ft of RU/EU); laboratories and material testing
Offices, banks, restaurants, hotels/motels, indoor movie/TV studios, schools, police/fire stations, utility work centers, electric substations, telecommunications hubs

Explosives, hazardous manufacturing: not listed in IU-1 (appear only in the IU-3 list, 33-264(3)). Data centers: not addressed. Solar: not addressed. General outdoor storage: not a standalone use; 33-260 requires operations/storage inside a building or within masonry walls at least 6 ft high.
conditional_uses: Asterisked uses (auto body, canning, cabinet shops, boat repair, fertilizer/insecticide storage, vulcanizing, welding, etc.): by right if 500+ ft from RU/EU (250 ft if fully enclosed, no openings facing); otherwise public hearing
Auto/truck sales on 10+ acres, outdoor backlots, religious facilities outside UDB: public hearing
Adult uses: special exception only, with 1,000/1,200/750 ft spacing

standards.min_lot_size: No general minimum stated in district article (auto/truck sales 2 acres; mixed-use hotel 5 acres)
standards.max_height: No fixed district height in article; Art. III: portions 35-40 ft set back 25 ft, then 1 ft per additional 5 ft; height not greater than width of widest abutting street without hearing (33-57, 33-58)
standards.setbacks: Art. II (33-51): front 20 ft; side street 15 ft (25 ft within 25 ft of RU/EU/GU); interior side 0 ft next to BU/IU, 5 ft with openings, 15 ft next to RU/EU/GU; rear 20 ft from residential boundary, 0/5 ft from business/industrial
standards.other: Landscaped open space 10% of net lot (15% if abutting residential; 20% for auto/truck sales); greenbelt 8 ft (sites to 3 acres) or 10 ft; operations enclosed in building or 6 ft masonry wall; administrative site plan review (33-310.4)

districts.notes: Item list is paraphrased from a mirror summary; some items not individually verified. Armories and arsenals are listed but this is not an energetics manufacturing use. A search summary reported that Chapter 13 (not Chapter 33) governs use and storage of explosives; not read.

districts.name: Industrial, Heavy Manufacturing District
districts.purpose: Heavy manufacturing district adding more intensive industrial uses to the IU-1 list. Purpose statement not found in the mirrored text.
permitted_uses: All IU-1 uses except adult entertainment, private schools and nonpublic educational facilities

Movie/TV studios with indoor stages and outdoor backlots; asphalt drum mixing plants under 150 tons/hr; rock and sand yards; cement and clay products; soap manufacturing (vegetable byproducts only); railroad shops; sawmills
Petroleum storage tanks up to 30,000 gal aggregate; larger only after public hearing or underground/in a rockpit
Dynamite storage (33-262 item 11) is permitted in IU-2; construction debris recovery transfer facilities in 15,000+ sq ft enclosed building

Explosives manufacturing, fireworks, ammunition: not listed in IU-2 (explosives, fireworks, guncotton etc. are listed only in IU-3 under 33-264(3)). Data centers, solar: not addressed. Outdoor storage: 33-263 requires storage inside building or within masonry walls at least 6 ft high. Truck terminals/storage garages: via IU-1 items 36 and 59.
conditional_uses: Industrial uses within 500 ft of RU, EU or BU-1 district require public hearing (250 ft if fully enclosed with no openings facing); petroleum tanks over 30,000 gal need hearing unless underground

standards.min_lot_size: Not specified in district article
standards.max_height: Same as IU-1 (Art. III 33-57, 33-58)
standards.setbacks: Art. II 33-51 as IU-1; petroleum tanks 300 ft from residential buildings
standards.other: Landscaped open space 10% (15% if abutting residential); greenbelt 8 ft/10 ft; no residential except caretaker quarters; administrative site plan review

districts.notes: Purpose and general lot size not found. Read via mirror summary. The 33-263(a) hearing trigger lists BU-1 as well as RU/EU.

districts.name: Industrial, Unlimited Manufacturing District
districts.purpose: Most permissive industrial district; allows IU-1 and IU-2 uses plus heavy and hazardous industries, with hazardous uses controlled case by case through Sec. 33-265.
permitted_uses: All IU-1 and IU-2 uses except adult entertainment, adult day care and private/nonpublic schools; caretaker/watchman quarters only with an existing industrial use

About 100 heavy and hazardous industries listed in 33-264(3), including: Explosives; dynamite storage; fireworks; guncotton; match manufacture and storage; nitrates of an explosive nature (manufacture and storage); pyroxylin; testing of jet engines and rockets; acids, ammonia, chlorine, caustic soda, phenol, calcium carbide; acetylene and hydrogen/oxygen manufacture; oil refining; radioactive waste handling; atomic reactor; refuse disposal; scrap metal reduction; plastic and synthetic resins; wood preserving; wet-cell batteries; insecticides/fungicides (depending on materials and quantities)

Ammunition and gunpowder: not named in the list as read. Data centers, solar: not addressed. Outdoor storage: 33-266.1 requires materials and operations inside a building or within 6-8 ft masonry walls. Truck terminals: via IU-1 item 59.
conditional_uses: All 33-264(3) hazardous uses are subject to 33-265: written application to Director, who assesses objectionable influences; high-hazard uses (fire, explosion, toxic gas, noise, vibration, dust, odor) require public hearing before the Community Zoning Appeals Board and County Commission; lower-hazard uses may be assigned to IU-3 or a less restrictive district
Any listed use within 500 ft of RU or EU requires public hearing (250 ft if fully enclosed with no openings facing)
Petroleum storage tanks need fire wall or dike (33-266)

standards.min_lot_size: Not specified in district article
standards.max_height: Same as IU-1 (Art. III 33-57, 33-58)
standards.setbacks: Art. II 33-51 as IU-1
standards.other: Landscaped open space 10% (15% abutting residential); greenbelt 8 ft/10 ft; structures above 4 stories need extra open space; enclosure rule; administrative site plan review; site plan valid 12 months

districts.notes: Key finding: explosives manufacture is listed as an IU-3 use but only after Director review under 33-265, and requires public hearing where explosion/fire hazard is high. Item numbering and the full list were read through a summary; verify exact wording on Municode before relying on it.

districts.name: Industrial District, Conditional
districts.purpose: District for large industrial projects and industrial parks on suitable tracts; must not be used for offensive or obnoxious uses (odor, gas, dust, noise, vibration, pollution).
permitted_uses: All IU-1 uses except adult entertainment and private schools
All IU-3 uses (excluding those specifically prohibited in IU-2) plus similar industrial uses

Residential prohibited except caretaker quarters

Explosives: not named, but IU-3 uses are included, so 33-264(3) hazardous uses are potentially available subject to the 33-269 permit review. Data centers, solar: not addressed. Outdoor storage: 33-270 requires operations and storage inside buildings or masonry walls.
conditional_uses: Use permit review (33-269): Director issues permits on a favorable agency report; no hearing mentioned in the text read; appeal under 33-311(C). Use is denied if detrimental to health/safety or offensive/obnoxious

standards.min_lot_size: Minimum tract 10 acres; 330 ft frontage and 330 ft depth; industrial park lots 125 ft by 150 ft

conditional_uses: Public hearing: studios with outdoor backlots; night clubs at least 500 ft from RU/EU
